review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib's AlgebraicTopology directory for product or pi results on the fundamental group, including `piMulEquiv` and `prodEquiv`. Mathlib has only the fundamental groupoid product iso (`FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.piIso` and `prodIso` in `FundamentalGroupoid/Product.lean`). It has no fundamental-group-of-a-product equivalence, so `FundamentalGroup.piMulEquiv` has no competing Mathlib declaration. The file builds on existing pieces: `MonoidHom.pi`, `FundamentalGroup.map`, `Path.Homotopic.pi` and the local `piProj`, `piAssembly` and `piProductIso`. I did not read the sibling `FundamentalGroupoid/Product.lean` in detail. That file's `piProductIso` may be a universe-generalised variant of Mathlib's `piIso`, but it is outside this target, and the supplied sources do not show a cost to the target from it. I did not look at the library's own `FundamentalGroup` file for internal duplication. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
